cvs: 'Black Magic' – near-black leaves · 'Mojito' – green speckled purple-black · 'Pink China' – pink stems, reputedly hardier · 'Fontanesii' – dark purple stems
foliage: herbaceous; very large arrow-shaped leaves that die back in winter
hardinessNote: Tender (H1b): RHS rates the species for a warm glasshouse, 10–15°C minimum. Outdoors only in summer; lift or bring in before frost.
prune: Remove tatty or scorched leaves as needed; cut away foliage when it collapses in autumn before storing the tuber.
resilience: Thrives in heat, humidity and shelter; leaves tear in wind, scorch in dry air and are killed by frost. Pests: red spider mite and aphids, mainly under glass.
soilWarning: Lift or protect before the first frost
sources: RHS 511667 (Colocasia esculenta 'White Lava' (Royal Hawaiian Series) (v)), search snippet: grown under glass; no size or rating in the snippet

toxicity: All parts are toxic if eaten raw, causing painful burning and swelling of the mouth and throat in children, cats and dogs; the sap can irritate skin and eyes, so wear gloves.
uncertain: latin: the label spelling 'Calocasia' has been corrected to the genus Colocasia. The species is assumed to be esculenta, which is the usual attribution for 'White Lava'. Verify.
hardiness: given as H1c from memory of RHS ratings for Colocasia esculenta. Some sources treat it as H2, and tubers may survive mulched in very sheltered gardens. Verify the RHS band.

height and spread: left blank because cultivar-specific figures are not known with confidence. Typical container-grown C. esculenta in the UK reaches around 1 m, but this needs checking for 'White Lava'.
visual: the description of white central splash and veins is from memory. Check exact patterning and leaf colour against a supplier image.
sunMin: estimated at part shade. Light shade is generally tolerated, but the exact lower limit is not established.
clay: left blank. It likes rich moist soil, but suitability for heavy clay as a bedding plant is not established.
compliance: no plant breeders' rights or other legal status for 'White Lava' is known. Check whether PBR applies.
cvs: sibling cultivars are listed from memory. The relative hardiness of 'Pink China' should be checked.
pestRisk and thirst: ratings are judged from general Colocasia behaviour, not cultivar data.
